title: Check and adjust the drive chain
exit_state: Chain free movement in range at the tightest point, both sides on the same mark, every nut torqued, chain lubricated.
completeness: Covers finding the tight spot, measuring at the rubbing strip, adjusting both sides equally, torques, recheck, brake check and lubrication.

required_tools.name: Stand that lifts the rear wheel

required_parts.name: Chain lubricant
required_parts.purpose: Triumph Performance chain lubricant or equal.

prerequisites: Chain clean enough to see the links.
critical_stop_conditions: Adjuster marks not the same both sides: the wheel is misaligned.
Spindle nut or lock nuts not torqued: do not ride.
Stiff links or damaged rollers: replace the chain.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Check, adjust and lubricate the chain after every race and whenever it looks dry. Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Lift the rear wheel
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand with the rear wheel off the ground and the rear suspension fully unloaded.
verification: Rear wheel off the ground, shock extended.

steps.title: Find the tightest point
steps.instruction: Turn the rear wheel slowly and find where the chain is tightest. Keep fingers away from the chain and sprocket.

steps.title: Measure the free movement
steps.instruction: At the tightest point, push the chain up directly above the end of the chain rubbing strip until it is taut, and measure from the swingarm surface to the lower edge of the chain at that point. It must be 55–58 mm (2.17–2.28 in).

steps.title: Loosen the axle
steps.instruction: Loosen the rear wheel spindle nut and the lock nuts on both chain adjuster bolts.
verification: Spindle nut and both lock nuts loose.

steps.title: Adjust both sides equally
steps.instruction: Turn both adjuster bolts by the same amount, using the adjuster marks as a guide: clockwise increases free movement, counterclockwise reduces it. Push the wheel firmly against the adjusters and check the same mark lines up on both sides.
verification: Same mark on both sides, wheel against the adjusters.

steps.title: Tighten
steps.instruction: Tighten both adjuster lock nuts to 25 N·m (18 lbf·ft) and the rear wheel spindle nut to 120 N·m (89 lbf·ft).
verification: Lock nuts and spindle nut torqued.

steps.title: Measure again
steps.instruction: Find the tightest point again and remeasure. It must still be 55–58 mm (2.17–2.28 in).
verification: Free movement in range after tightening.

steps.title: Check the rear brake
steps.instruction: Spin the wheel: it must turn freely, then stop firmly when you press the pedal.
verification: Rear brake works and does not drag.

steps.title: Clean and lubricate
steps.instruction: If the chain is dirty, clean it first, never with a pressure washer. Apply chain lubricant to the sides of the rollers and leave the bike standing, ideally overnight, so it soaks in. Wipe off the excess before riding.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the free movement found and set, the adjuster mark used and the date.

title: Check chain, sprocket and rubbing strip wear
exit_state: Chain, sprockets and sliders measured and inspected, worn parts identified, results recorded.
completeness: Covers damage check, 20-link stretch measurement, sprocket wear and rubbing strip and slider inspection with fastener torques.

required_tools.name: Stand that lifts the rear wheel

required_parts.name: Drive chain
required_parts.purpose: DID 520DMA4K SDH, 114 link non-O-ring, if replacement is needed.

required_parts.name: Rubbing strips or sliders
required_parts.purpose: If worn.

prerequisites: Chain cleaned.
critical_stop_conditions: Chain over the limit or damaged: do not ride.
Missing or worn-through slider: the chain will cut the frame or swingarm.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Check chain, sprockets and rubbing strips every 15 operating hours. Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Lift the rear wheel
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand with the rear wheel off the ground and the rear suspension unloaded.

steps.title: Look for damage
steps.instruction: Turn the wheel slowly and check every link for damaged rollers, loose pins and stiff links. Never try to free a stiff link; it means the chain is finished.

branches.label: Damaged
branches.condition: Any damaged roller, loose pin or stiff link.

steps.title: Stretch and measure
steps.instruction: Hang a moderate weight on the chain to pull it taut. On the straight run, measure from the centre of one pin to the centre of the pin 20 links further on. Measure in several places, because chains wear unevenly. Replace the chain if any length exceeds 317.5 mm (12.5 in).

steps.title: Check the sprockets
steps.instruction: Turn the wheel and look at both sprockets for hooked, uneven or damaged teeth.

branches.label: Sprockets worn
branches.condition: Worn sprockets: replace both sprockets with the chain, since a new chain on worn sprockets wears out fast.

steps.title: Check the rubbing strips
steps.instruction: Inspect the chain rubbing strip on the swingarm and the upper and lower sliders for wear, cracks and missing pieces. If a rubbing strip or slider is worn, cracked or missing, replace it: upper slider to engine fastener 10 N·m (89 lbf·in), upper slider guard to frame fastener 25 N·m (18 lbf·ft), lower slider fastener 10 N·m (89 lbf·in) with a new fastener.
verification: Strips and sliders sound, any replaced part torqued.

steps.title: Plan the replacement
steps.instruction: If anything failed, fit a new chain (DID 520DMA4K SDH, 114 link non-O-ring) and sprockets as a set, then set the free movement with the chain adjustment guide. A chain that breaks or jumps off can lock the rear wheel.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the 20-link lengths, sprocket and slider condition and anything replaced.

title: Check brake fluid, pads and discs
entry_state: Bike on level ground, brakes cool.
exit_state: Fluid at the marks, pads and discs inside their limits, firm lever and pedal.
completeness: Covers fluid levels and top-up, pad measurement and change, disc thickness and run-out checks and bedding in.

required_tools.name: Soft tool to push pistons back

required_parts.name: Brake fluid
required_parts.purpose: DOT 4 from a sealed container.

required_parts.name: Brake pads
required_parts.purpose: Full set per wheel when worn.

required_parts.name: Cable ties
required_parts.purpose: Two new ones for the rear master cylinder cover.

prerequisites: Rags over paint: brake fluid strips it.
critical_stop_conditions: Soft or spongy lever or pedal: do not ride.
Pad at or below its minimum: replace before riding.
Disc cracked or out of limits: do not ride.
Never get fluid, wax or lube on the discs.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Check brake fluid levels, pads and discs after the first operating hour and every 15 operating hours, and before every race. Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Check the front fluid
steps.instruction: Turn the bars so the front reservoir is level and look at the sight glass on the reservoir. Fluid must reach the upper level mark.

steps.title: Check the rear fluid
steps.instruction: Hold the bike upright on level ground and look at the sight glass on the rear master cylinder. Fluid must reach the top of the glass.

steps.title: Top up
steps.instruction: Cover painted parts. Front: clean the cap, remove its small fasteners, cap and diaphragm, fill to the upper line with new DOT 4 fluid from a sealed container, refit with the diaphragm seated and tighten the fasteners gently. Rear: remove the two cable ties and the master cylinder cover, clean round the cap, remove the cap with its O-ring and diaphragm, fill to the upper line, refit the cap at 17 N·m (13 lbf·ft) and refit the cover with new cable ties. A clear drop since last time means worn pads or a leak.

steps.title: Measure the front pads
steps.instruction: Look into the caliper and measure each pad including its carrier plate. Replace both front pads if either is at or under 3.7 mm (0.15 in).

steps.title: Measure the rear pads
steps.instruction: Measure the rear pads including carrier plate: the inner pad must be more than 4.5 mm (0.18 in) and the outer pad (with its insulator and shim) more than 6.4 mm (0.25 in).

branches.label: Pads at the limit
branches.condition: Any pad at or under its minimum.

steps.title: Change the pads
steps.instruction: Pads are always changed as a set per wheel. Open the reservoir, push the old pads back to retract the pistons without letting fluid overflow, remove the two R-clips and the retaining pin and take the pads out. Check the anti-rattle spring (rear: arrow pointing forward) and the sliding plate are in place, fit the new pads, the pin and the R-clips the same way round. Pump the lever or pedal until firm, set the fluid level and close the reservoir (rear cap 17 N·m (13 lbf·ft)). Use pads with the correct carrier plate thickness; thin aftermarket backing plates can fall out of the caliper.
verification: New pads fitted, lever and pedal firm, levels set.

steps.title: Check the discs
steps.instruction: Look for cracks and damage, then measure thickness at several points on the braking surface. Front service limit 2.7 mm (0.11 in), rear 3.6 mm (0.14 in). Run-out, measured with a dial gauge, must not exceed 0.05 mm (0.002 in) front and 0.05 mm (0.002 in) rear.

branches.label: Disc out of limits
branches.condition: Cracked, too thin or too much run-out: replace the disc before riding.

steps.title: Bed in new parts
steps.instruction: After new pads or discs, ride with care and avoid hard braking until they have bedded in.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down fluid levels, pad thicknesses, disc readings and what was replaced.

title: Set the rear brake pedal height and free play
exit_state: Pedal at the chosen height with correct free play, lock nuts torqued, no drag.
completeness: Covers free play check, pedal height, push rod setting and drag check.

required_tools.name: Stand that lifts the rear wheel

prerequisites: Brakes cool.
critical_stop_conditions: No free play at the pedal: do not ride, the brake can overheat or lock.
Brake dragging after release: correct before riding.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down why the pedal is being adjusted (height preference, too much or too little free play).

steps.title: Check the free play
steps.instruction: Press the pedal down by hand between the toe-piece fasteners until you feel resistance. Free play at the pedal must be 6–9 mm (0.24–0.35 in); the push rod itself needs at least 1 mm (0.04 in), which is roughly the pedal free play divided by six.

branches.label: Free play correct and height fine
Change needed
branches.condition: Wrong free play or a new height wanted.

steps.title: Unhook the return spring
steps.instruction: Detach the return spring from the pedal.

steps.title: Back off the push rod
steps.instruction: Loosen the master cylinder push rod lock nut and turn the push rod for maximum free play.

steps.title: Set the pedal height
steps.instruction: Loosen the lock nut on the pedal height adjuster screw, turn the screw for the height you want, then hold it and tighten the lock nut to 10 N·m (89 lbf·in). The adjustment range is small; too low a pedal may not give enough free play.

steps.title: Set the push rod
steps.instruction: Turn the push rod until the adjuster screw touches the frame, then back it off by one and a half turns. Hold it and tighten its lock nut to 10 N·m (89 lbf·in).
verification: Push rod set, lock nut torqued.

steps.title: Refit the spring and recheck
steps.instruction: Hook the spring back on and check the pedal free play is 6–9 mm (0.24–0.35 in). Adjust the height again if it is not.

steps.title: Check for drag
steps.instruction: Lift the rear wheel, spin it, press and release the pedal and spin it again. It must turn freely without the brake dragging. A pedal with no free play overheats the brake.
verification: No drag after releasing the pedal.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the free play and any change of height. Get used to a new pedal position before racing.

title: Pre-ride check
exit_state: Every item checked, faults fixed or the bike parked until they are.
completeness: Covers frame, steering, fork, brakes, tyres, wheels, oil, coolant, clutch, throttle, chain, fuel, air filter, fasteners and stop switch.
excluded: Any repair found necessary (see the matching guide)
prerequisites: Engine cold for the coolant check.
critical_stop_conditions: Any crack, leak, soft brake or sticking throttle: do not ride.

steps.title: Frame, swingarm and bar
steps.instruction: Look over the frame welds, subframe and engine mounts, footrests, swingarm welds and mounts, and the handlebar near its clamps for cracks or bends. Damaged frame, swingarm or bar parts are replaced, never repaired.

steps.title: Steering and fork
steps.instruction: Turn the bars lock to lock: smooth, not loose, and no cable binding. Pump the fork with the front brake on: smooth, no leaks at the seals.

steps.title: Brakes
steps.instruction: Pull the lever and press the pedal: both firm, not spongy, not travelling too far. Check both fluid levels at their marks and enough pad left.
verification: Lever and pedal firm, levels correct.

steps.title: Tyres and wheels
steps.instruction: Check cold tyre pressures front 14 psi (0.97 bar), rear 14 psi (0.97 bar), tread wear and cuts. Check the rims for dents and squeeze the spokes for any loose one.
verification: Pressures set, tyres and wheels sound.

steps.title: Oil and leaks
steps.instruction: With the bike upright and level, check the oil in the sight glass and look under the engine for any oil, coolant or fuel leak.

steps.title: Coolant
steps.instruction: Engine cold: coolant 10 mm (0.39 in) above the radiator fins.

steps.title: Clutch
steps.instruction: Clutch fluid at the upper line and no leaks; lever action smooth.

steps.title: Throttle
steps.instruction: Throttle opens smoothly and snaps shut on its own; free play 2–3 mm (0.08–0.12 in).

steps.title: Chain
steps.instruction: Chain clean, lubricated, free movement 55–58 mm (2.17–2.28 in) at the tightest point, no stiff links.

steps.title: Fuel and air filter
steps.instruction: Enough fuel and no leaks. Fill no higher than 35 mm (1.38 in) below the filler neck, so the fuel has room to expand. Air filter clean and seated.

steps.title: Fasteners and stop switch
steps.instruction: Check the obvious fasteners and hose clamps are tight. Start the engine and check the stop switch shuts it off.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours and anything found or fixed. Any fault found must be put right before riding.

steps.instruction: Turn the bars lock to lock: smooth, not loose, and no cable binding. Pump the fork with the front brake on: smooth, no leaks at the seals.

steps.title: Brakes
steps.instruction: Pull the lever and press the pedal: both firm, not spongy, not travelling too far. Check both fluid levels at their marks and enough pad left.
verification: Lever and pedal firm, levels correct.

steps.title: Tyres and wheels
steps.instruction: Check the cold tyre pressures against your recorded setting, tread wear and cuts. Check the rims for dents and squeeze the spokes for any loose one.
verification: Pressures set, tyres and wheels sound.

steps.title: Oil and leaks
steps.instruction: With the bike upright and level, check the oil in the sight glass and look under the engine for any oil, coolant or fuel leak.

steps.title: Coolant
steps.instruction: Engine cold: coolant 10 mm (0.39 in) above the radiator fins.

steps.title: Clutch
steps.instruction: Clutch fluid at the upper line and no leaks; lever action smooth.

steps.title: Throttle
steps.instruction: Throttle opens smoothly and snaps shut on its own; free play 2–3 mm (0.08–0.12 in).

steps.title: Chain
steps.instruction: Chain clean, lubricated, free movement 55–58 mm (2.17–2.28 in) at the tightest point, no stiff links.

steps.title: Fuel and air filter
steps.instruction: Enough fuel and no leaks. Never fill into the filler neck; leave room for the fuel to expand. Air filter clean and seated.

steps.title: Fasteners and stop switch
steps.instruction: Check the obvious fasteners and hose clamps are tight. Start the engine and check the stop switch shuts it off. Check the side stand folds up and is held by its rubber strap.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours and anything found or fixed. Any fault found must be put right before riding.

title: Pre-ride check
exit_state: Every item checked, faults fixed or the bike parked until they are.
completeness: Covers frame, steering, fork, brakes, tyres, wheels, oil, coolant, clutch, throttle, chain, fuel, air filter, fasteners and stop switch.
excluded: Any repair found necessary (see the matching guide)
prerequisites: Engine cold for the coolant check.
critical_stop_conditions: Any crack, leak, soft brake or sticking throttle: do not ride.

steps.instruction: Look over the frame welds, subframe and engine mounts, footrests, swingarm welds and mounts, and the handlebar near its clamps for cracks or bends. Damaged frame, swingarm or bar parts are replaced, never repaired.

verification: Lever and pedal firm, levels correct.

steps.title: Tyres and wheels
steps.instruction: Check cold tyre pressures for off-road use front 14 psi (0.97 bar), rear 14 psi (0.97 bar) (mixed off-road and road: front 22 psi (1.52 bar), rear 26 psi (1.8 bar); road: front 36 psi (2.48 bar), rear 36 psi (2.48 bar)), tread wear and cuts. Check the rims for dents and squeeze the spokes for any loose one.
verification: Pressures set, tyres and wheels sound.

steps.title: Oil and leaks
steps.instruction: With the bike upright and level, check the oil in the sight glass and look under the engine for any oil, coolant or fuel leak.

steps.title: Coolant

steps.title: Clutch
steps.instruction: Clutch fluid at the upper line and no leaks; lever action smooth.

steps.title: Throttle

steps.title: Chain
steps.instruction: Chain clean, lubricated, free movement 55–58 mm (2.17–2.28 in) at the tightest point, no stiff links.

steps.title: Fuel and air filter

steps.title: Fasteners and stop switch
steps.instruction: Check the obvious fasteners and hose clamps are tight. Start the engine and check the stop switch shuts it off. Check the side stand folds up and is held by its rubber strap.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours and anything found or fixed. Any fault found must be put right before riding.

title: Wash the bike and check it afterwards
exit_state: Bike clean and dry, airbox dry, chain lubricated, brakes tested.
completeness: Covers covering openings, hand washing, drying, airbox check, brake disc care, lubrication, fork seal wipe and drying run.

required_parts.name: Chain lubricant
required_parts.purpose: For after washing.

prerequisites: Engine and exhaust cold.
critical_stop_conditions: Water in the airbox: do not start until it is dry.
Brakes weak after washing: do not ride.

steps.title: Before washing
steps.instruction: Let the engine cool. Plug the exhaust outlet with a plastic bag and rubber band, cover the airbox intake, and bag the levers and switch housings.

steps.title: Wash gently
steps.instruction: Use cold water with a mild motorcycle cleaner and a soft sponge. Never use a pressure washer or steam cleaner, and never spray near the air intake, electrical parts, brake calipers and master cylinders, switch housings, steering head, suspension seals, under the tank or at the wheel bearings. Do not pressure-wash the radiator fins or the chain.
verification: Bike washed by hand without pressure.

steps.title: Uncover and dry
steps.instruction: Remove the bags and covers, clear the intake and dry the bike with a cloth so water does not stand on it.
verification: Covers off, intake clear, bike dry.

steps.title: Check the airbox
steps.instruction: Open the air filter cover panel and check no water got past the filter. Wet foam or water in the airbox means the filter must be cleaned and dried before the next start.

branches.label: Water inside
branches.condition: Clean and dry the filter and airbox before starting.

steps.title: Brakes
steps.instruction: Never wax or lubricate the discs; clean them only with an oil-free brake cleaner. Test both brakes before riding.

steps.title: Lubricate
steps.instruction: Dry and lubricate the chain, then check its free movement is 55–58 mm (2.17–2.28 in). Lightly lubricate pivots, bolts and nuts.

steps.title: Fork seals
steps.instruction: Wipe the fork tubes and the dust seals clean; dirt left under the seals causes leaks.

steps.title: Run the engine
steps.instruction: Outdoors, start the engine and let it run for a few minutes to drive out moisture. Do not use it to dry a hot exhaust.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Note anything found while washing: cracks, leaks, loose parts, worn grips.

title: Check the spokes, rim run-out and tyre seating
entry_state: Bike cool, on a lift stand.
exit_state: Every spoke tight at its torque, rims inside the run-out limit, tyre and rim lock correctly seated, recorded.
completeness: Covers spoke inspection, the ring test, tightening spokes in stages to torque, measuring rim run-out, spotting a slipped tyre and refitting the tube and rim lock.
excluded: Spoke replacement and wheel truing or rebuilding

required_tools.name: Spoke wrench from the tool kit
Dial gauge on a truing stand
Something to tap the spokes with

required_parts.name: Inner tube
required_parts.purpose: New one if the tyre has slipped on the rim.

prerequisites: Bike stable on a lift stand with the wheel off the ground.
critical_stop_conditions: Damaged or bent spoke: do not ride, have it replaced.
Spokes cannot be brought to torque or run-out over the limit: the wheel needs rebuilding by a wheel builder.
Never tighten a spoke nipple more than half a turn at a time.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Spokes and rim run-out are checked after the first operating hour and every 15 operating hours. Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Lift the wheel
steps.instruction: Raise the bike on a lift stand so the wheel turns freely off the ground. Do the same check on both wheels.
verification: Wheel off the ground, bike stable.

steps.title: Look at every spoke
steps.instruction: Turn the wheel slowly and look for bent or damaged spokes and dents in the rim.

branches.label: Bent or damaged spoke
branches.condition: Do not ride; have the spoke replaced by a specialist and record it.

steps.title: Ring test
steps.instruction: Tap each spoke briefly. A tight spoke gives a clear ringing note; a loose one sounds flat. Mark the loose ones.

steps.title: Tighten loose spokes in stages
steps.instruction: With the spoke wrench and a spoke torque wrench, tighten each loose nipple to 6 N·m (53 lbf·in), but never more than half a turn (180°) at a time: if it needs more, stop at half a turn and move to the next loose spoke, then come back round. Repeat until every spoke rings.
verification: All spokes at 6 N·m (53 lbf·in) and ringing.

steps.title: Check rim run-out
steps.instruction: After any spoke tightening, check run-out with the tyre off and the wheel on a truing stand (or in the bike without the brake caliper fitted). Measure side-to-side (axial) and up-and-down (radial) run-out with a dial gauge. Limit: 1.8 mm (0.07 in) each way, front and rear.
verification: Axial and radial run-out within 1.8 mm (0.07 in).

branches.label: Run-out over the limit
branches.condition: The wheel must be rebuilt by a specialist wheel builder.

steps.title: Check the tyre has not slipped
steps.instruction: Look at the inflation valve: it should point straight at the hub. If it leans, the tyre has slipped on the rim and can pull the valve out.

steps.title: Refit the tube and rim lock
steps.instruction: Loosen the rim lock, take the tyre off, throw the inner tube away and fit a new one, refit the tyre, position the rim lock and tighten its nut to 12 N·m (9 lbf·ft).
verification: New tube fitted, rim lock at 12 N·m (9 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Set the pressures
steps.instruction: Set the cold tyre pressures to the figure for your bike (see the pre-ride check). After new tyres or tubes, check the pressures and the seating again 24 hours later.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down which spokes needed tightening, the run-out readings and anything replaced or booked in.

title: Check the steering head, wheel bearings and fork
entry_state: Bike on level ground, stand available.
exit_state: Steering head, wheel bearings and fork checked, findings recorded.
completeness: Covers the steering head play check, wheel bearing rock and spin checks and the fork pump and leak check.
excluded: Steering head bearing adjustment and lubrication
prerequisites: Bike stable on its stand.
critical_stop_conditions: Any steering head or wheel bearing play: do not ride until it is put right.
Fork leaking or binding: do not ride.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Steering head bearings are checked after the first operating hour and then at every service, more often when racing; wheel bearings every 15 operating hours. Write down the date and hours.

steps.title: Lift the front
steps.instruction: On level ground, put the bike on a stand with the front wheel off the ground and make sure it cannot tip. Do not rock the wheels hard during these checks: the bike can fall off the stand.
verification: Front wheel off the ground, bike secure.

steps.title: Check the steering head for play
steps.instruction: Stand in front of the bike, hold the bottom of both fork outer tubes and try to push them forward and back. Then turn the bars lock to lock: they should move freely.

branches.label: Play or tight spots
branches.condition: Note it: steering head bearing adjustment is a dealer job and must be done before riding.

steps.title: Check the front wheel bearings
steps.instruction: Stand at the side and gently rock the top of the front wheel from side to side, then spin it. Play in the hub, noise or rough turning means the bearings must be replaced.

steps.title: Check the rear wheel bearings
steps.instruction: Move the stand so the rear wheel is off the ground and repeat the rock and spin check on the rear wheel.

steps.title: Check the fork
steps.instruction: With the bike back on the ground, hold the bars, apply the front brake and pump the fork up and down several times. It should move smoothly without roughness or excessive stiffness. Check each leg for damage, scratches on the sliding tube and oil leaks.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the result for the steering head, each wheel bearing and the fork, and book any bearing or fork work before the next ride.

title: Check the steering head, wheel bearings and fork
entry_state: Bike on level ground, stand available.
exit_state: Steering head, wheel bearings, seals and fork checked, findings recorded.
completeness: Covers the steering head play check, wheel bearing rock and spin checks, bearing seal inspection and the fork pump and leak check.
excluded: Steering head bearing adjustment and lubrication
prerequisites: Bike stable on its stand.

Fork leaking or binding: do not ride.

steps.title: Lift the front
steps.instruction: On level ground, put the bike on a stand with the front wheel off the ground and make sure it cannot tip. Do not rock the wheels hard during these checks: the bike can fall off the stand.
verification: Front wheel off the ground, bike secure.

steps.instruction: Stand in front of the bike, hold the bottom of both fork outer tubes and try to push them forward and back. Then turn the bars lock to lock: they should move freely.

branches.label: Play or tight spots
branches.condition: Note it: steering head bearing adjustment is a dealer job and must be done before riding.

steps.instruction: Stand at the side and gently rock the top of the front wheel from side to side, then spin it. Play in the hub, noise or rough turning means the bearings must be replaced.

steps.title: Check the rear wheel bearings

steps.title: Check the wheel bearing seals
steps.instruction: Look at the bearing seals on both wheels for damage or wear; worn seals are replaced.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the result for the steering head, each wheel bearing and the fork, and book any bearing or fork work before the next ride.

title: Remove and refit the front wheel
entry_state: Bike cool, on a lift stand.
exit_state: Front wheel refitted with the spindle and clamps at torque, fork free, brake working.
completeness: Covers retracting the pads, removing the spindle and wheel, greasing the spacers and spindle, refitting, the torque order for the nut and clamp bolts and the brake check.
excluded: Tyre, tube, bearing or disc replacement

required_tools.name: Soft tool to push the pads back

required_parts.name: High temperature grease
required_parts.purpose: Spacer faces and spindle.

prerequisites: Bike stable on a lift stand with the front wheel off the ground.
critical_stop_conditions: Brake lever soft after refitting: pump it firm before moving the bike.
Never lever against the disc, caliper or pad lining.

steps.title: Lift the front
steps.instruction: Raise the bike on a lift stand so the front wheel is off the ground. Keep brake fluid off the bodywork.

steps.title: Push the pads back
steps.instruction: With a soft tool, gently push the brake pads into the caliper to retract the pistons. Never lever against the disc or the pad lining.

steps.title: Remove the spindle and wheel
steps.instruction: Remove the spindle nut, loosen the four spindle clamp bolts, support the wheel and pull the spindle out from the right side. Lift the wheel out and take the two spacers out of the hub.

steps.title: Grease and fit the spacers
steps.instruction: Put a thin layer of high temperature grease on the spacer faces that touch the bearing seals and fit both spacers to the hub.

steps.title: Fit the wheel and spindle
steps.instruction: Put the wheel between the fork legs with the disc inside the caliper. Grease the outside of the spindle thinly, but not the face that bears on the spacer, and slide it in.
verification: Disc in the caliper, spindle through.

steps.title: Tighten the spindle nut
steps.instruction: Fit the spindle nut and, holding the spindle, tighten it to 60 N·m (44 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Let the fork settle
steps.instruction: Lower the bike to the ground and pump the fork a few times so the left leg settles in its natural position on the spindle.

steps.title: Tighten the clamp bolts in order
steps.instruction: Tighten the outer spindle clamp bolts to 19 N·m (14 lbf·ft), then the inner ones to 19 N·m (14 lbf·ft), then the outer ones again to 19 N·m (14 lbf·ft).
verification: All four clamp bolts at 19 N·m (14 lbf·ft) in the right order.

steps.title: Clean the disc and check the brake
steps.instruction: Clean and degrease the disc, pump the lever until firm and check the front brake works and the wheel turns freely.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours and why the wheel was removed.

title: Remove and refit the rear wheel
entry_state: Bike cool, on a lift stand.
exit_state: Rear wheel refitted, chain free movement set, spindle at torque, brake working.
completeness: Covers retracting the pads, removing the spindle, chain and wheel, greasing the spacers and spindle, refitting with the adjuster blocks, setting the chain and torquing the spindle.
excluded: Tyre, tube, bearing, sprocket or disc replacement

required_tools.name: Soft tool to push the pads back

required_parts.name: High temperature grease
required_parts.purpose: Spacer faces and spindle.

prerequisites: Bike stable on a lift stand with the rear wheel off the ground.
critical_stop_conditions: Brake pedal soft after refitting: pump it firm before moving the bike.
Never ride with the spindle not at its torque.

steps.title: Lift the rear
steps.instruction: Raise the bike on a lift stand so the rear wheel is off the ground. Keep brake fluid off the bodywork.

steps.title: Push the pads back
steps.instruction: With a soft tool, gently push the brake pads into the caliper to retract the pistons.

steps.title: Remove the nut and adjuster block
steps.instruction: Remove the spindle nut and washer and take off the chain adjuster block on that side.

steps.title: Take the chain off
steps.instruction: Push the spindle through just far enough to let the wheel move forward, push the wheel fully forward and lift the chain off the rear sprocket.

steps.title: Remove the wheel
steps.instruction: Support the wheel, pull out the spindle with its adjuster block and lift the wheel out. Take the two spacers out of the hub.

steps.title: Grease and fit the spacers
steps.instruction: Put a thin layer of high temperature grease on the spacer faces that touch the bearing seals and fit both spacers.

steps.title: Fit the wheel
steps.instruction: Put the wheel in the swingarm with the disc inside the caliper. Grease the outside of the spindle thinly, but not the face that bears on the spacer. Fit the adjuster block and spindle, put the chain on the sprocket, then fit the other adjuster block, washer and nut without tightening. Make sure both adjuster blocks sit up against the adjuster screws.
verification: Wheel in, chain on, nut loose, blocks against the screws.

steps.title: Set the chain
steps.instruction: Check the chain free movement (55-58 mm (2.17-2.28 in) at the tightest point) and adjust if needed, with the same adjuster mark on both sides (see the chain guide).
verification: Chain free movement correct, marks equal.

steps.title: Tighten the spindle
steps.instruction: Tighten the rear spindle nut to 120 N·m (89 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Check the brake
steps.instruction: Pump the pedal until firm and check the rear brake works and the wheel turns freely.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours and why the wheel was removed.

title: Set up the handlebar, levers and shift pedal
entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine off.
exit_state: Bar height and reach, lever span and shift pedal set for the rider, fasteners at torque, throttle checked at full lock.
completeness: Covers handlebar height, moving the bar to the forward reach position, brake and clutch lever span and the shift pedal position.
excluded: Throttle cable routing and free play adjustment (see the throttle guide)

required_parts.name: Thread locker
required_parts.purpose: Lower bar clamp bolts when the clamp is turned (ThreeBond 1324 or equivalent).

prerequisites: Bike stable on a stand.
critical_stop_conditions: Engine speed changes when the bars are turned: correct the throttle cables before riding.
Shift pedal touching anything through its travel: reposition it.
Never adjust controls while riding; try new settings in a safe area first.

steps.title: Record the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down the bar position (mark on the bar against the clamp), lever span settings and shift pedal position, so you can go back.

steps.title: Remove the bar pad
steps.instruction: Undo the hook-and-loop strips at the back of the bar pad, release the cover and lift the pad off.

steps.title: Set the bar angle
steps.instruction: Loosen the four upper clamp fasteners until the bar turns, rotate it to the angle you want within the degree marks on the bar, then tighten the four fasteners to 25 N·m (18 lbf·ft) in the Triumph clamp tightening sequence.
verification: Bar set, clamp at 25 N·m (18 lbf·ft).

branches.label: Also want the forward reach
branches.condition: The bar comes from the factory in the rear position; it can be moved 9 mm (0.35 in) forward.

steps.title: Move the bar forward
steps.instruction: Note the bar alignment mark, remove the four fasteners and the upper clamp and lift the bar out, keeping the brake and clutch master cylinders upright (a helper helps). Hold the nuts under the lower clamp and remove its bolts, refit the rubber bushes if they came out, turn the lower clamp round 180°, clean the bolt threads and old thread locker from the nuts, apply thread locker and tighten the riser bolts to 40 N·m (30 lbf·ft) while holding the nuts. Refit the bar and upper clamp, line up the alignment mark and tighten the four fasteners to 25 N·m (18 lbf·ft) in the Triumph clamp tightening sequence for the forward position.
verification: Lower clamp turned, risers at 40 N·m (30 lbf·ft), clamp at 25 N·m (18 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Check the throttle at full lock
steps.instruction: Refit the bar pad. Start the engine and, at idle, turn the bars to full left and full right lock: the idle speed must not change. If it does, correct the throttle cable routing and free play before riding.

steps.title: Set the lever span
steps.instruction: Turn the span adjuster on the brake lever and on the clutch lever to bring each lever to a comfortable reach; fully counterclockwise gives the shortest reach. Then lift the front wheel, check it turns without the brake dragging, apply and release the brake and check again.
verification: Both levers set, front brake not dragging.

steps.title: Set the shift pedal
steps.instruction: Stock position is with the mark on the pedal lined up with the mark on the selector shaft. To change it, remove the pinch bolt and the pedal, clean both splines, line the splines up so the pedal sits where you want it, refit it and tighten the pinch bolt to 10 N·m (89 lbf·in). Work the pedal up and down: it must not touch anything.
verification: Pedal set, pinch bolt at 10 N·m (89 lbf·in), free through its travel.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the new bar, lever and pedal settings, and ride them in a safe area first.

title: Clean and grease the side stand
entry_state: Bike raised and supported, side stand up.
exit_state: Side stand clean, greased, new split pin fitted, spring hooked on and returning the stand fully.
completeness: Covers removing the spring and stand, cleaning and inspecting, greasing the friction and pivot surfaces and refitting with a new split pin.
excluded: Side stand bracket or frame repair

required_parts.name: Split pin
required_parts.purpose: New one every time.

required_parts.name: General purpose grease
required_parts.purpose: For example Triumph Performance RG2 (NLGI 2).

prerequisites: Bike raised and supported so it cannot fall.
critical_stop_conditions: The spring is under tension: wear eye protection and release it slowly.
Stand does not snap fully up: do not ride.

steps.title: Raise the bike
steps.instruction: Raise and support the bike so it cannot fall, with the side stand up.

steps.title: Unhook the spring
steps.instruction: Wearing eye protection, unhook the spring from its upper mount and take it off the spring bracket, letting it go slowly.

steps.title: Remove the stand
steps.instruction: Remove and throw away the split pin, collect the washer, pull out the pivot pin and take the stand off.

steps.title: Clean and inspect
steps.instruction: Clean all old grease and dirt off the friction and pivot surfaces of the stand, the bracket and the pivot pin. Replace any part that is damaged or badly worn.

steps.title: Grease and refit
steps.instruction: Put a thin layer of general purpose grease on the friction and pivot surfaces of the stand, bracket and pivot pin. Line the stand up with the bracket, fit the pivot pin, the washer and a new split pin and fold its ends over.
verification: Stand refitted with a new split pin.

steps.title: Refit the spring
steps.instruction: With the stand up, hook the spring on the spring bracket and then onto the upper mount, wearing eye protection. Check the stand swings freely and snaps fully up.

steps.title: Record
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours and anything replaced.
